title: Agentic AI changes the trust boundary
points: A model proposes actions; the application and tools perform them
Separate user, agent, model, retrieval, tool and protected data roles
Every tool call crosses an authorization and data boundary
Human approval is a control for consequential actions
diagram: User to agent; model proposes tool call; policy gate and optional human approval precede tool, then observation returns to agent.
remember: A model suggestion is not authorization.

title: Bedrock Agent orchestration loop
points: InvokeAgent can use preprocessing and orchestration
The agent may retrieve knowledge, request missing parameters or invoke an action group
A tool result becomes an observation that informs another iteration
The session returns a response after sufficient evidence
diagram: Question→agent→model decision; branch to knowledge base or action group; observation loops back; final response exits.
remember: An agent can iterate; it is not a fixed three-step pipeline.

title: Action groups are executable contracts
points: Define function or API parameters in action-group schema
Fulfillment can use Lambda or return control to the application
Validate types, resource IDs, tenancy and business rules in the executor
Use least privilege and idempotent handling for retries
diagram: Agent action group schema→parameter validation→Lambda OR return-control application executor→business system.
remember: The tool implementation enforces the contract.

title: Knowledge retrieval is not tool permission
points: Knowledge Bases return scoped evidence for grounding
Action groups can change external state
Retrieved content is untrusted input, not an instruction to bypass controls
Separate read access from write capability and track provenance
diagram: Parallel retrieval read lane and action write lane; explicit authorization gate before write.
remember: A document cannot grant the agent new privileges.

title: Agent service role and Lambda permission
points: Bedrock Agents service role needs only approved model, KB and action integration access
Action-group Lambda needs a resource policy permitting the agent to invoke it
Lambda execution role separately scopes downstream actions
Caller needs InvokeAgent on intended alias
diagram: Four identities with labeled permissions, not one universal role.
remember: Permission to invoke a tool differs from the tool’s own permissions.

title: Return control keeps execution in the app
points: RETURN_CONTROL sends elicited parameters and invocationId to the application
Application checks policy and approval before executing an API
Submit the result with matching invocationId and action group in a later InvokeAgent request
Handle denial, timeout and replay explicitly
diagram: Agent→application invocationInputs; app policy/approval→external API; app result→agent via sessionState; denied branch returns no execution.
remember: Return control makes the application the execution boundary.

title: User confirmation before high-impact action
points: Configure confirmation for selected Bedrock Agent action-group functions
Present exact target, parameters and consequence to the user
Deny must prevent the action; never execute first and ask later
Revalidate authorization and resource state after approval
diagram: Proposed action→confirmation→allowed branch→fresh validation→tool; denied branch→safe response.
remember: Approval belongs before the side effect.

title: AgentCore Identity: inbound and outbound
points: Inbound auth verifies who may invoke the runtime or gateway
Outbound credentials enable scoped access to AWS or third-party tools
User-delegated and machine-to-machine credentials serve different ownership models
Avoid embedding long-lived API keys in prompts or agent code
diagram: Caller identity→AgentCore inbound→agent; separate outbound credential provider→tool.
remember: Authentication into an agent does not authorize every tool.

title: Gateway authorization before tool calls
points: AgentCore Gateway exposes governed tool targets
IAM or JWT protects entry; a policy engine can authorize tool actions
Default deny and caller/resource conditions limit tool reach
Keep schema validation and downstream permissions in place
diagram: Agent→authenticated Gateway→policy decision→tool target; denied branch stops before target.
remember: One governed gateway does not remove downstream checks.

title: Three identities in delegated tool access
points: Distinguish end user, agent workload and outbound service credential
Preserve caller context where the pattern supports it
Use dedicated scopes, consent and expiry for external SaaS access
Audit who requested and which credential executed the operation
diagram: User principal→agent identity→credential provider→external tool, each with explicit scope.
remember: A shared agent role can hide the real requester without context propagation.

title: Guardrails evaluate input and output
points: Configure content, denied topic, word and sensitive-information policies
Input and output intervention behavior differs
A guardrail can attach to supported agent/model paths
Test policy versions with representative prompts and responses
diagram: User input→input guardrail→model→output guardrail→response; blocked branches explicit.
remember: A guardrail is one layer, not an access policy.

title: Prompt injection crosses a data boundary
points: An attacker can place instructions in retrieved documents or tool results
Treat those bytes as data even when the model reads them
Use scoped retrieval, output checks, tool authorization and confirmation
Test exfiltration and unintended action attempts
diagram: Attacker document→retrieval→agent; attempted tool call→policy/approval gate denies.
remember: Untrusted content must not become tool authority.

title: Automated reasoning has a narrow proof scope
points: Policy-backed checks can flag contradiction and unstated assumptions
Validation is limited to variables represented in the policy
It does not detect prompt injection or off-topic material
Current documented limitations include English US and no streaming
diagram: Response→policy logic check→structured feedback; separate prompt-attack filter and human review.
remember: A valid policy result is not a universal truth guarantee.

title: Responsible AI is a lifecycle
points: Define intended use, affected users and unacceptable harms
Evaluate accuracy, harmful content, bias and privacy on representative cases
Monitor incidents and drift after release
Assign owners, version evidence and escalation paths
diagram: Design→test→release gate→monitor→revise loop, with human owner at each decision.
remember: Safety needs continuous measurement and ownership.

title: Human review must be meaningful
points: Show source evidence, proposed action, target and impact
Reviewer can approve, reject or request more information
Record decision, identity, time and policy version
Protect against rubber-stamping, stale context and dual-control bypass
diagram: Agent proposal→reviewer evidence panel→approve/reject/revise; only approved path reaches executor.
remember: A click without context is not effective oversight.

title: Step Functions approval with callback
points: A Standard workflow can pause using a callback task token
Deliver approval request through an application/notification channel
Authorized decision returns the token and outcome
Set timeout, denial, duplicate and expired-token behavior
diagram: State machine→wait for callback→approved action OR rejected close; timeout branch escalates.
remember: The workflow must resume only from an authorized callback.

title: Approval and automation need failure boundaries
points: Expired approval must not trigger execution
Retries must avoid duplicate side effects
Changed target state requires fresh pre-action validation
Record partial failures and compensating or manual recovery
diagram: Failure branches around approval token, validation, executor, and audit record.
remember: Approval of old parameters is not approval of changed reality.

title: Agent trace and protected evidence
points: InvokeAgent traces show orchestration, KB queries and action group steps when enabled
CloudTrail records supported API activity; application logs record business decisions
AgentCore telemetry settings vary by resource and signal
Redact secrets and protect prompt, tool and trace data
diagram: Agent runtime→trace; API→CloudTrail; business approval→protected audit store, distinct evidence streams.
remember: A trace explains a path; it is not an access-control boundary.

title: Choose agent or deterministic workflow
points: Use an agent when open-ended interpretation and tool selection are required
Use Step Functions for known, durable and auditable state transitions
Combine them: agent proposes, workflow validates and obtains approval
Bound latency, cost, retries and blast radius
diagram: Three independent patterns: direct API, agent selection, deterministic workflow; combined handoff for controlled execution.
remember: Do not make a deterministic approval process depend on model discretion.

title: Walkthrough: deny injected export request
points: Retrieved document contains malicious export instruction
Agent tries to propose an external tool call
Gateway policy and app validation deny unauthorized destination
Trace records attempt; user receives grounded answer without export
diagram: Query→retrieval with injected instruction→proposed export→deny gate; no tool execution.
remember: The data source cannot rewrite the tool policy.

title: Walkthrough: approve a scoped refund
points: Agent proposes exact account, amount and refund reason
Policy caps and reviewer context determine approval
Step Functions callback pauses before executor
Executor rechecks order and idempotency; audit captures outcome
diagram: Proposal→policy→review callback→fresh validation→refund API→receipt; denial/timeout separate.
remember: The approved payload must match the executed payload.

title: Walkthrough: investigate an agent denial
points: Inspect caller authentication and resource policy first
Review Gateway policy denial and outbound credential scope
Compare trace, request ID and target service rejection
Fix the narrowest missing permission and retest denied paths
diagram: Caller→agent→gateway→tool with four diagnostic checkpoints; no automatic blanket grant.
remember: A tool error is not always a model problem.
